name: GA-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Nikema Williams running with a large fundraising edge

model.rationale: GA-05's D+36 lean and Williams's incumbency and fundraising advantage make this a Safe D seat; markets price a Democratic win at roughly 98%. No polls or ratings suggest any reason to move from the fundamentals.
model.watch: Only an unexpected scandal or a major redistricting change would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Atlanta-based GA-05 is one of the most Democratic-leaning House districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+36. Incumbent Nikema Williams is running for reelection after easily securing her party's nomination, and she has raised nearly $600,000 for the race. Republican nominee John Oscar Salvesen reports no fundraising figures, leaving Williams with a decisive financial edge.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, but prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 98 percent. With the fundamentals, money, and market pricing all aligned, the district remains safely Democratic.
